title: Gideon and the Summit
premise: August Joubert, a disgraced mountain guide hiding in a fishing village, discovers a tide-revealed cave holding relics of the Meridian Company, which once ruled the highlands through violence and now quietly owns everything above the snowline. The cave's map points to the river's forbidden source, where the Company buried proof of its founding massacre—and August realizes her blacklisting was engineered by the man who wrote that history. Pursued by the Company's fixers, she follows the river upstream with an orphaned stonemason's apprentice and a retired ranger who once betrayed her. At the source, she must choose between destroying the evidence to free the valleys or trading it for her own reinstated name; she burns it publicly instead, letting the truth belong to everyone, and finally finds belonging not in a clean reputation but in the community that walks down from the mountain beside her.
about_author: Hazel Pemberton is a former alpine rescue volunteer who writes adventure fiction from a drafty cottage in the Cairngorms. Her novels are known for ruthless landscapes, morally tangled heroes, and rivers that refuse to be followed politely.

chapters.title: The Lowest Tide in Forty Years
chapters.summary: August Joubert, scraping by as a boat-mender in the village of Greyharbor, watches an unprecedented low tide expose a sea cave locals call the Devil's Ledger. POV: August. Emotional beat: restless curiosity overriding her hard-learned instinct to stay invisible.

chapters.title: What the Cave Kept
chapters.summary: Inside the cave August finds ledgers, a brass compass engraved with her father's initials, and a map tracing the river Vell upstream to a source marked with the Meridian Company's seal. POV: August. Emotional beat: grief and suspicion—her blacklisted past may have been manufactured.

chapters.title: A Debt with Teeth
chapters.summary: August's creditor, harbormaster Corvin, demands payment within a month; meanwhile strangers in Company grey arrive asking about cave-treasure. She realizes the map is worth more than her life. POV: August. Emotional beat: cornered pragmatism—she decides to climb before they decide for her.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Who Wouldn't Stay
chapters.summary: Fourteen-year-old Tam, an orphaned stonemason's apprentice, catches August stealing rope and blackmails his way into her expedition, claiming the Company razed his family's quarry. POV: alternating August/Tam. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of shared grievance.

chapters.title: Grey Coats at the Ford
chapters.summary: Company fixers ambush them at the river ford; August's old climbing partner, retired ranger Ede Vasq, appears and drives them off—then reveals he testified against August years ago under coercion. POV: August. Emotional beat: fury, then the bitter arithmetic of needing him anyway.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: The three follow the Vell into gorge country; Ede teaches Tam rivercraft while August tests whether Ede's remorse is real. They find a drowned Company survey camp, recently searched. POV: Ede. Emotional beat: guilt made useful—he wants to pay a debt he can never fully repay.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge at Marrowfen
chapters.summary: In a Company-owned town, they pose as surveyors; August sees her own wanted notice, freshly reprinted with a higher bounty. An innkeeper who remembers her father quietly feeds them and warns of checkpoints ahead. POV: August. Emotional beat: the shock of being remembered kindly despite her ruined name.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Crimes
chapters.summary: Reading the cave ledger by firelight, they learn the Meridian Company's fortune was built on a massacre at the river's source—the 'Founding Accord'—and that August's father was the surveyor who refused to falsify its records. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: awe and anger; the mountain's history is a crime scene.

chapters.title: Whitefall Crossing
chapters.summary: A storm forces them across a collapsing snow bridge; Tam nearly dies, and August saves him using techniques her father taught her. Ede confesses the full shape of his betrayal. POV: August. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into trust—the team becomes real on the ice.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owns the Sky
chapters.summary: They're captured by Warden Halloway, the Company executive who orchestrated August's blacklisting; he offers her reinstatement, wealth, and her father's restored honor if she surrenders the map. POV: August. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened into clarity—she sees exactly what power costs.

chapters.title: Escape from the High Camp
chapters.summary: Tam sabotages the camp's supply lines; Ede takes a beating covering their escape. They flee into a hidden valley where outlaws and exiles live beyond Company law—a whole society of the blacklisted. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: wonder—for the first time, people like them are the majority.

chapters.title: The Republic of the Ridgeline
chapters.summary: In the free valley, August meets Sefa, her father's old expedition mate, who confirms the source hides the original Founding Accord documents. The exiles debate: destroy them, publish them, or bargain. POV: August. Emotional beat: belonging offered—but on the condition she stop walking alone.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: Sefa agrees to guide them only if August promises the documents go to the valley, not to any crown or court. August hesitates—justice feels safer in official hands. POV: August. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes: can justice exist outside the law?

chapters.title: Halloway's Rope
chapters.summary: Halloway's fixers find the valley using a tracker planted on Ede during his capture; skirmish breaks out, and the exiles' granary burns. Ede offers himself in exchange for the valley's safety. POV: Ede. Emotional beat: sacrifice as penance, refused by August at gunpoint.

chapters.title: The Stair of Names
chapters.summary: Sefa leads them up a hidden route carved by pre-Company climbers, each step etched with names of the massacred. August finds her father's name among the carvers, not the dead. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: reverence—August inherits a lineage she never knew she had.

chapters.title: Above the Map's Edge
chapters.summary: Past the last marked point, they climb uncharted ice as Halloway's party closes below. The compass, they realize, doesn't point north—it points to the source itself, tuned by her father. POV: August. Emotional beat: terror and inheritance fused; the mountain is testing her.

chapters.title: The Source of the Vell
chapters.summary: At a glacial vault they find the sealed archive: the Founding Accord, massacre orders, and her father's refusal letter. Halloway arrives with hostages from the valley, offering one final trade. POV: August. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible symmetry—everything she lost, priced against everyone she loves.

chapters.title: Burn It Where They Can See
chapters.summary: August refuses both surrender and secrecy: she reads the Accord aloud over a signal mirror relay visible to the valley, then burns the originals so no one—not Company, crown, or exile council—can own the truth again. POV: August. Emotional beat: triumphant defiance; justice delivered outside every law.

chapters.title: Descent Under Judgment
chapters.summary: Halloway orders his men to open fire; some refuse, the lie of his authority cracking. In the chaos Ede falls saving Tam. The survivors descend through a storm, pursued by nothing but consequence. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: grief and hard-won courage side by side.

chapters.title: The Trial Nobody Presided Over
chapters.summary: Word outruns them downriver; villages along the Vell rise, tolls burn, and Halloway is arrested not by courts but by dockworkers who read August's words secondhand. Greyharbor turns out to meet her at the ford. POV: August. Emotional beat: vindication that feels strange because it came from people, not papers.

chapters.title: Ede's Grave Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: They bury Ede where the Stair of Names begins, adding his name to the rock. Corvin forgives August's debt without being asked; Tam is apprenticed to Sefa. POV: August. Emotional beat: mourning braided with gratitude—the cost made visible and honored.

chapters.title: Gideon and the Summit
chapters.summary: August learns 'Gideon' was her father's trail-name, carved atop the summit cairn; she climbs alone to finish his route and leaves the compass there, pointing home. She returns to Greyharbor not cleared, but chosen—as guide, neighbor, and keeper of the story. POV: August. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging earned, not granted.
